ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 1620 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported eight major and about one hundred and seventy minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.34; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: ‘of Chicago’ was turned into the wedding’s location; the speaker and addressee of unit 729 were inverted; the rain and voices simile (723) was lost; the Sheik song (615) lost its meaning and rhyme; and ‘anh’ in Jordan’s narration was ambiguous (601–613); all corrected.
‘I’m not?’ became ‘Không sao?’ and lost its meaning; now ‘Tôi không chăm sóc cô ấy nữa à?’.
Nick’s question ‘Anh chắc là muốn em đi chứ?’ read as spoken by Daisy; it is ‘…muốn tôi đi chứ?’.
Catherine was written as Myrtle’s elder sister (units 1407, 1459 and 213); she is the younger.
Missing verb, lexical slips, addressee errors and calques in the early chapters were corrected over three rounds.
The Southern drunk-speech spellings in units 434–441 are rendered with only light marking.

summary: Full assessment of all 1,620 English/Vietnamese passages: the epigraph and Chapters I–IX, from Nick’s father’s advice to the boats against the current. The first reviews scored 8.30, 7.975, 8.625 and 8.425 across four ranges and found six majors, mostly pronoun and speaker confusions, a lost song and a mistaken kinship; a revision applied every finding and recast the prose, and a second round of fresh separate-context reviews found two further majors (a misread speaker and the sisters’ order) that were corrected. The last fresh reviews scored 8.75 (units 1–465), 8.80 (466–926), 8.675 (927–1342) and 8.75 (1343–1620) with no major or critical finding, and the remaining minor points were then applied. The final score is taken from the weakest range, 8.675 on the half-point scale, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. No unresolved major or critical issue remains.

title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Gatsby vĩ đại’ is this edition’s own rendering; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.
